ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The left figure is a stair shape composed of two rectangles, with the left vertical side labeled x; the short horizontal side at the top is labeled 11; the horizontal side at the middle step is labeled 13. There are gray cutting lines in the figure, one connecting the lower-left corner to the upper inner corner point, and another connecting the lower-left corner to the black point on the right side, dividing the original figure into three parts. The right figure shows these three parts rearranged into an arrow-shaped figure, in which there is a long horizontal line segment extending all the way to the rightmost tip. Reasoning: Label the points in the left figure according to the method in the problem: the lower-left corner is A, the upper-left corner is B, the top inner corner is C, the step corner is D, the upper-right corner is E, and the lower-right corner is F. From the left figure, BC = 11, DE = 13, AB = x can be read. After rearrangement, triangle ABC is rotated; its original side AB, that is, the left vertical side of length x, becomes in the right figure that long horizontal line segment leading to the rightmost tip. This long horizontal line segment can be regarded as being pieced together from the original step horizontal side DE and the original entire bottom side AF. DE = 13. The original bottom side AF spans the widths of two rectangles, whose widths correspond to 11 and 13 respectively, so AF = 11 + 13 = 24. Therefore x = DE + AF = 13 + 24 = 37.

Now read that same long horizontal segment in the second diagram as being made of two adjoining original edges: the marked step edge DE of length 13, followed by the bottom edge AF of the whole original shape.
